chunks: And whatever is narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah be pleased with him - from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi Al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan. And I have also narrated it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to Ibrahim ibn Hashim
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I have narrated it, indicating the author's direct transmission
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ali ibn Ibrahim, a major narrator in Shia hadith collections
key_terms.مَاجِيلَوَيْهَ: Majilawayh, a key scholar and teacher of Ibn Babawayh
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, a prominent early Shia narrator

ai.seo_question: How did Ibn Babawayh verify the authenticity of narrations from Muhammad ibn Sinan?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous methodology in verifying the reliability of his primary source, Muhammad ibn Sinan, by cross-referencing two distinct transmission chains. By tracing the narrations through both Majilawayh and his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, al-Saduq ensures the authenticity of the legal rulings derived from this key Kufi scholar, reflecting the Shia emphasis on rigorous *isnad* analysis in hadith compilation.
